review.reviewBody: I used to spend hours every week ordering food. Now it's simple, super easy, and I have free time to spend on other aspects of my restaurant.

@graph.name: Three steps, and nothing inside Entree changes
@graph.description: You export lists, we set up the accounts, and kitchens begin sending orders.

step.name: Export your lists
step.text: A spreadsheet out of the system you have is plenty. Items and prices per account go into a single admin screen under the codes you use.

step.name: We set up each account
step.text: We load each guide and set the account up, then the kitchen downloads the app. Most send something in before the day is out.

step.name: The order lands finished
step.text: The customer has approved it, and it carries an order number and the time it was sent, in the format your system takes.

@graph.name: Do we need a NECS Entree alternative so accounts can speak what they need?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and we would rather lead with that. Entree is the software your company runs on; VoiceOrder Solutions handles how an order gets in. Keep the first, add the second, and the real question becomes which part of the day you are trying to fix.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than NECS Entree?

acceptedAnswer.text: At getting an order out of a kitchen that will not use an order form, yes. At everything else Entree does, the question does not apply. We have no ledger, no payables, no warehouse module and no proof of delivery, which is exactly why we belong next to it.

@graph.name: Doesn't Entree already have customer ordering?

acceptedAnswer.text: It does. They offer web order entry and mobile order entry, plus a rep order pad. All of it works by a person finding items and typing quantities. The accounts who were never going to do that are the ones our app is for.

@graph.name: Is Entree hooked up to VoiceOrder Solutions?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Nothing links the two products, and neither vendor supports the other. Our orders leave in the formats shown above. Which of those your Entree setup can take in directly is something to check in the demo. We do not promise it here.

@graph.name: Will this touch our installation or our version?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We never need a login to your Entree system to set this up. We work from an export of your item lists, and orders arrive as an email attachment or over EDI or the API. Your version, your upgrade schedule and your support arrangement are all unaffected.

@graph.name: How fast could this be live?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most distributors this goes live inside 24 to 48 hours, and most kitchens get a first order in that day. There is no project here, because nothing in Entree is connected or changed. So adding a step beside it asks far less of you than a NECS Entree alternative that replaces the ERP.

Neither of us publishes figures. We quote per distributor. Since Entree stays, the decision is only what we cost on top of it. That is a far narrower call than choosing the platform the whole company depends on.

@graph.name: Where do the Entree details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Read off necs.com on 10 October 2026: the module list, the 1987 founding date and the web, mobile and rep ordering products. They publish no price and no implementation process, so this page guesses at neither. If any detail is now out of date, that error is ours.
